text: Add impression-time request-context fields tab, hour, and weekday to the neutral user/video additive scorer; the measured train-only temporal screen reports a +0.00221 primary lift with full coverage and positive lift on all four holdout dates.
rationale: This is the most directly supported candidate: screen:request_context measured a positive aggregate primary lift of 0.002213 with 100% coverage and positive daily lifts on every screened date. The change is small, ranking-relevant, and easy to isolate.
exact_ablation: Add only the impression-time request_context fields tab, hour, and weekday; keep the additive user/video model, optimizer, loss, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase, approximately +0.002 to +0.004, because the screened feature group improved within-user discrimination.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small increase or flat, approximately -0.001 to +0.002, because the screening showed stronger GAUC evidence than top-five evidence.

text: Replace the additive user/video scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP scorer while retaining only user_id and video_id inputs, testing whether nonlinear identity interactions improve within-user ordering.
rationale: The neutral seed cannot represent nonlinear user-item effects. The measured request-context screen shows that impression-time context contains incremental ranking signal, supporting a broader test of nonlinear ranking capacity even though this candidate deliberately isolates architecture rather than adding that feature family.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive linear scoring function with a compact embedding-plus-MLP scorer over the existing user_id and video_id inputs; do not add request-context features or change the loss.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely modest increase, approximately 0 to +0.003, if nonlinear user-item affinity is present.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely flat to modestly positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.003; nonlinear separation may not consistently alter the top five.

text: Add a low-rank explicit cross branch over user/video IDs and request context to the embedding-plus-MLP ranker, isolating bounded-order context interactions.
rationale: The request-context screen is the only measured positive direction, and its benefit may depend on user- or item-specific context effects rather than additive offsets. Explicit crosses directly test that mechanism while preserving the deep branch.
exact_ablation: Add only one two-layer low-rank cross branch over the existing feature vector and concatenate it with the unchanged MLP output; keep features, loss, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase by approximately 0 to +0.003 if context changes user/video preferences.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potentially larger relative benefit than GAUC, approximately 0 to +0.004, if the interactions correct top-rank choices; otherwise it may be flat.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with within-group RankNet pairwise loss on valid positive-negative displayed groups, targeting the GAUC ordering objective directly.
rationale: The official objective contains within-user pairwise ordering, while the seed uses pointwise BCE. The measured request-context evidence indicates useful ranking signal exists, making a ranking-aligned loss a plausible next test, but group construction and pair coverage create substantial implementation risk.
exact_ablation: Replace only pointwise BCE with within-user RankNet pairwise loss using four sampled negatives per positive within intact training candidate groups; keep the seed feature set and model architecture unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: More likely positive than nDCG@5, approximately +0.001 to +0.005, if mixed-label groups are sufficiently common.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely flat to positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.004; sampled pairs may improve broad ordering without fixing top-rank errors.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with mixed-group ListNet top-one loss to emphasize competition among displayed candidates and top-five ranking quality.
rationale: The screened request-context gain is stronger for GAUC than nDCG@5, suggesting a complementary top-ranking intervention may be valuable. ListNet is a materially distinct listwise objective, though its value depends on reliable intact candidate groups and adequate mixed-label coverage.
exact_ablation: Replace only pointwise BCE with ListNet top-one loss on intact mixed-label groups; retain the seed user/video features, additive model, optimizer, and training schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Flat to modestly positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.003, because group normalization may sacrifice some broad calibration.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potentially positive, approximately +0.001 to +0.005, if the displayed groups are valid and top-rank competition is learnable.

text: Use user-normalized BCE instead of impression-weighted BCE so prolific users or long candidate groups do not dominate training.
rationale: The official GAUC is within-user and positive-count weighted, so changing the reduction may improve alignment with the evaluated population. The positive request-context screen provides a useful signal for this reweighting test, but no direct measured evidence establishes the weighting effect.
exact_ablation: Change only the BCE reduction to exact inverse candidate-count weighting with equal total weight per complete user candidate group; keep features, additive architecture, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely small increase or flat, approximately 0 to +0.003, if the current fit is dominated by prolific users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Uncertain and possibly slightly negative, approximately -0.002 to +0.002, because pointwise group normalization does not explicitly target top ranks.

text: Encode the screened request context as learned categorical embeddings rather than additive one-hot weights, allowing compact nonlinear context effects without changing the user/video scorer.
rationale: The request-context group has full coverage and positive lift on every screened date, but its aggregate effect is variable. A compact learned representation may capture interactions among tab, hour, and weekday more efficiently than independent additive weights.
exact_ablation: Add only learned embeddings for tab, hour, and weekday and concatenate their pooled representation to the seed scorer; do not add other fields, interaction layers, or loss changes.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase of approximately 0 to +0.003 if context categories have nonlinear effects.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely flat to modestly positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.003, with gains dependent on context-specific candidate ordering.

text: Add only an hour-of-day cyclic representation from the request context, testing whether smooth temporal preference variation is more useful than independent hour categories.
rationale: The measured request-context group is positive, but the available screen aggregates tab, hour, and weekday. A single-field decomposition can determine whether hour is the main transferable signal while keeping the experiment narrowly interpretable.
exact_ablation: Add only sine and cosine encodings of impression hour to the seed user/video features; omit tab and weekday and change nothing else.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely small positive or flat, approximately -0.001 to +0.002, if temporal preference is smooth.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely flat to small positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.002, because smooth time effects may improve separation below the top ranks.

text: Add only tab as an impression-time categorical feature to the additive scorer, isolating the strongest operational component of request context without adding hour or weekday.
rationale: The full request-context screen measured a +0.00221 primary lift with full coverage and consistent positive daily direction. This narrow decomposition is lower-risk and can reveal whether tab alone carries enough of that measured signal to justify broader context expansion.
exact_ablation: Add only the tab field to the seed user/video additive features; do not add hour, weekday, or any other context field.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely small positive or flat, approximately -0.001 to +0.002, because tab is only part of the screened group.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely flat to small positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.002.

text: Add only weekday as an impression-time categorical feature to the additive scorer, isolating weekly preference differences from the other request-context fields.
rationale: The request-context screen showed positive lift on all four dates, but did not identify field-level attribution. Weekday is a clean, low-cost single-field ablation that tests whether calendar effects contribute ranking signal.
exact_ablation: Add only weekday to the seed user/video additive features; do not add tab, hour, or any other context field.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely near flat to small positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.0015, because weekday is a limited subset of the measured signal.

text: Train the seed scorer with a pairwise margin objective only on request-context-conditioned within-user pairs, testing whether context-supported ordering benefits from a ranking-specific optimization target.
rationale: This combines the strongest measured feature direction with a distinct ranking loss, but keeps the comparison interpretable as a single objective replacement relative to a context-enabled pointwise formulation. The screen establishes that request context is promising; it does not establish pairwise-loss gains, so confidence is limited.
exact_ablation: Replace only BCE with within-user RankNet loss while adding the already screened request_context fields as the fixed feature set for both compared implementations; no architecture or sampling change beyond the loss replacement.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potentially positive, approximately +0.001 to +0.005, if context separates positive-negative pairs within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potentially positive but less certain, approximately -0.001 to +0.004, depending on whether sampled pairs reflect top-rank errors.

text: Use a shallow residual MLP head on top of request-context features and user/video embeddings, replacing the additive scorer to learn context-dependent nonlinear preference shifts.
rationale: The measured request-context direction is positive but has daily variability larger than its mean lift. A small residual nonlinear head is a bounded architecture change intended to model stable context-by-identity effects without the capacity and risk of a deep cross network.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive scoring head with one two-layer residual MLP over user/video embeddings plus tab, hour, and weekday embeddings; keep pointwise BCE, optimizer, and feature availability policy unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely modest positive, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, if nonlinear context personalization is stable across time.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely flat to modestly positive, approximately 0 to +0.004, with potential top-rank gains from context-specific interactions.
